In this podcast episode, I speak with Canadian Broadcast LEGEND George Stroumboulopoulos, on how he's willingly chosen the hard path for 30+ years and remained at the very forefront of his craft. Interviewing some of the worlds' biggest celebrities, politicians and personalities - what it's like to maintain this level and when to call it quits. 

George Stroumboulopoulos:
IG: https://www.instagram.com/strombo/
YT: https://www.youtube.com/@TheStromboShow/videos

I've wanted to have this conversation for a LONG time. Strombo" is someone I grew up watching on MuchMusic. Speakers corner, channel 29! This were the days :) Now, he's sitting across from me in my studio and we're just… talking. LOL life is wild. We chat creating, independence, about choosing the harder path and not being mad about it.

He's been streaming since 1995 before anyone knew what that meant (or most of you were even alive) why the 'learning loop' is the most dangerous thing for creatives, and how he deals with people who've literally made TV shows trying to take him down. Spicy. His answer to that one stuck with me. It's a fun one, appreciate you being here!

Epidemic Sound, get after it and start your free trial: https://bit.ly/2KJwcVG

As many of you know I have been working on a documentary for Angels and Airwaves for some time now. I am not going to lie; this project was much more involving than I had ever anticipated. I operate in a world where spending 3-4 weeks on a single project is considered a very long time and when I set out to shoot this documentary, I thought it would be no exception - I was wrong.  Drowning in hours and hours of amazing footage paired with the fact that so much time has passed since this project kicked off due to COVID, I needed a bit of a refocus, a fresh perspective if you will. In this video I drop by Matti’s office to get his take on the realities of shooting a documentary. As always he helped me reset my expectations and get me back on track - what a guy! Should we get another office together??? Let me know in the comments!

Knowing when to quit is one of the most challenging things to figure out in life. In this video I talk a bit about this as it pertains specifically to the path I’ve taken. Many of you know that I have a burning passion for the art of leather craft and some of you may even know that I even had a leather business before pursuing a career on YouTube. At the time I didn’t know it, nor did I want to admit it but sometimes no matter how hard you work at something, it may not work out. There are times in life where you need to set whatever that something is that you love aside, as it may just not be the right time for it. You see, no matter how hard I tried at my leather business it just never really took off. I had given it my all and now, years later, I sit back and remember that the day I decided to move on was the same day I started my YouTube channel. Lately I have really been feeling the urge to get out my leather tools and supplies and set up a little area in my garage so that I can get back to tinkering and use this hobby as an outlet. I find that I now have a new appreciation for working with leather, and that it serves a different, healthier purpose in my life then it did years ago. It is now the outlet that I can use to disconnect, reflect, and use to slow down from the career I love. A BIG thank you to my buddy Jeff for building me an amazing bench in literally a day.  It’s so important to have a thing other than your thing, so that you don’t get sick of the thing that is your thing - watch the video and it will all make sense I PROMISE!

Today we are talking about how to make a killer After Effects intro for your videos!
Building a new intro is one of my ABSOLUTE favourite things about kicking off a new year. I’ve received a lot of comments on my new intros throughout the years and also a lot of questions from you on how to build a good intro. I walk you through an example from start to finish so that you can follow along and then take these techniques and maybe apply some of them to footage that is relevant to you and your channel. I also talk about what ingredients I think make for a good YouTube video intro and give you some things to think about and consider when you are making yours. I cannot believe this year is already coming to a close - where the heck did 2021 go!? In this video I take some time to reflect on the year, on the channel and on life. I also leave you with some final thoughts as I prepare for 2022. First off, next year I am going to commit to creating the videos that I normally second guess and talk myself out of. Why? Making vids is about the fun and enjoyment I have creating them and exploring these ideas fosters even greater creativity - PLUS I think a bunch of you are going to have a lot of fun watching them. It is important to follow through on your creativity as it’s just too easy to go down the road of making content that is EXPECTED of you versus content that you are passionate about. This is a battle each one of us creators constantly face. Finally, the largest takeaway and best advice I will leave you with is DON’T follow influence, follow your PASSION. Passion is what gave you the drive and has helped you achieve all that you have so far, so it only makes sense to keep following it! Buckle up because 2022 is going to be a fun one!

For the love of the art. A few weeks ago this philosophy had never been more apparent to me then while I was shooting a fun little intro using stop motion animation for a Youtube short. I couldn’t believe the amount of work involved to obtain just a couple seconds of incredible footage and it had me thinking – Why? Why take the time when there are so many easier methods? The answer - we do it for the LOVE of the art. Loving what we do is really what fuels us to push ourselves further and put in the extra time and effort to get better at our craft. Then I thought how fun it would be to go and visit someone who lives by this - Kevin Parry, a BEAST in stop motion animation and check out first-hand, his passion for this craft and the enormous amount of effort he puts into his work. In this video we visit Kevin at his home studio as he walks us through the incredible attention to detail and the meticulous planning that is required in creating stop motion animation. Just seeing his passion and love for his art left me so inspired and energized to think of ways for me to hone in and push myself even further. Thank you Kevin for having me, you have left me with such an appreciation for your craft, your passion and for your love of the art!

In this video we get our hands on the new DJI Mavic 3 Cine Premium Combo drone. If you are a cinematographer and are looking for a portable drone with all the features to help you capture the shot and remove some human error, this is it. Equipped with a dual-camera system featuring a Hasselblad 4/3 CMOS camera with 12.8 stops of dynamic range and a 28x zoom lens. The battery life has now been enhanced to deliver a flight time of up to 46 minutes, so with all 3 batteries that is over two hours of total flight time! The DJI Mavic 3 Cine also supports 10-bit D-log and is capable of shooting in 5.1K/50fps Apple ProRes 422HQ and even has a 1TB built-in SSD which is so convenient for when you go to fly and realize you forgot to bring a memory card – I can’t be the only one who has done this. Finally, I am very excited to try out all the intelligent features that are coming like: Hyperlapse, Mastershots, FocusTrack, QuickShots, Panorama as well as 4K/120fps and 4G transmission capability which will all be available through a firmware update in January 2022. #DJIMavic3 #Mavic3 #DJI #DJIDrone #ImageAboveEverything. @djiglobal

GOPRO HERO 10 : https://gopro.com

Introducing the new GoPro Hero 10. In this video I put this new GoPro to the ultimate action camera test – how? I phoned Red Bull. You guys know, I have not been a big fan of GoPro action cameras in the past as I could never really get the footage to look as great as they do in the promo videos. It is 2021, enter the new GoPro Hero 10  and I have to say, I am converted. The new HyperSmooth 4.0 stabilization is nothing short of incredible. I used footage straight out of the camera, no post stabilization needed, just right onto the timeline. I mounted this camera to some fairly unstable areas so you can see test footage on just how much it can handle. With the help from the new GP2 processor, you can shoot 240fps at 2.7K or even 5.7K at 60fps – this capability coming out of a little cube of a camera – INSANE! In this video I really focused on video capabilities here but on the photography side, which I want to do a dedicated video on, the new Hero 10 is capable of 23MP photos and also can pull 19MP stills from high res footage – WOW! Let me know what you think and if you are going to be upgrading your action cam with the new GoPro Hero 10!

Canon R3 Here: https://bit.ly/3CeIaQv

In this video we put the new Canon EOS R3 to the ultimate test. With its high-speed continuous shooting up to 30fps we needed a couple of MONSTER subjects to help us test its limits. Bring in the 2007 Porsche 911 GT3 RS, some would argue one of the last true analog RS 911s – what a car! However, this was not enough. Our friends at BMW Canada were gracious enough to supply us with another ABSOLUTE weapon of a subject – the 2022 BMW M5 CS. A car this big should not be able to move this quickly - 627hp folks and the sound, OMG. The new Canon EOS R3 is incredibly fast but I was also equally impressed with the new vehicle detection AF feature, as long as the camera can frame the full vehicle, it just locks on to it, making shooting cars that much easier – no matter how fast they are…trust me! Finally, we mounted the Canon R3 prototype on a drone - Why? Why not? Enjoy!

pVr_h0-i0UA.description:
Seadoo Switch: https://bit.ly/3gSbqnQ

In this video we test out the first-ever Sea-Doo Switch Pontoon boat. You all know how much I love my Sea-Doo GTX so when Sea-Doo let me try out their new Switch Pontoon boat I didn’t really know what to expect. I was lent the Sea-Doo Switch Cruise model with the 170 engine for a week and all I can say is that I am converted! A modular main deck that lets you change the seating/table layout in seconds, a rear swim platform with a bench and ladder and an audio system, this thing has all the ingredients for a great day out on the water. All it takes is for you to get behind the handlebars, yes handlebars, which by the way are exactly like my Sea Doo GTX and piloting the Switch is just like a big Sea-Doo - ZERO learning curve. The Sea-Doo Switch is not what you typically think of when thinking about a pontoon - it is agile and maneuvers so well, its quicker than I ever would have thought, and it has reverse and brakes!! Watch the video and see how a single Sea-Doo Switch brings Sea-Doo life personal watercraft fun to so many more people!

100MM Macro RF :
CANADA: https://bit.ly/3a8xmrk
 USA: https://bit.ly/2OPYi7W

You all know how much I love a good 100mm macro lens, in fact I think it’s my favourite lens. I’m so excited that Canon will finally be releasing their RF version soon and today I get to test it out. Honestly, Canon just needed to retain the capability from the latest EF version and create an RF version but they actually went ahead and made the lens even better. In this video we have a little fun as I test this new macro lens by taking some detailed shots of subjects around the office with the new Canon RF100mm 2.8 L Macro IS USM. Remember Macro lenses aren’t just limited to delivering close detail shots, however with this lens you do get a new minimum focus distance of 0.86ft and 1.4x magnification. Fun fact, I think I have used a 100mm macro lens for more portrait shots than any other lens, it is just such a great lens to shoot with. Finally, we have a look at the new Spherical Aberration (SA) control ring and I show you some examples of how this feature allows you to better shape the foreground and background bokeh. Let’s get into it!
